LESSON: READING 3.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.2: Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we read?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a text of about 300 words for comprehension
2. apply appropriate reading skills to obtain both factual and inferential information from a text

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 3.2.1 INTENSIVE READING: COMPREHENSION
This lesson teaches Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension for Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. read a text of about 300 words for comprehension
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. apply appropriate reading skills to obtain both factual and inferential information from a text
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension above.
2. Explain Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 3.2.1 Intensive Reading: Comprehension important for a Grade 4 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we read?
2. How can we read faster?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. read a text of about 300 words for comprehension
2. apply appropriate reading skills to obtain both factual and inferential information from a text

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
